findings.reason: the exclusion rests on a false fact about existing routing, so the author's scope decision may leave the second repair-verb run class unowed while believing it is already covered.
findings.text: §3 says `exited-unfinished` is out of scope because "such a run is already owed as `turn-ended-early`", but that duty kind is produced only for the classification `interrupted` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:53-58` keys `INTERRUPTED_RUN_PHASE`, and its recovery verb is `redispatch`); resolving the two readings on the current tree gives `exited-unfinished: verb='repair' duty_kind=''` against `interrupted: verb='redispatch' duty_kind='turn-ended-early'`, so an exited-unfinished run is owed nothing today

findings.reason: a worker implementing the deliverable as written fails its own done-when, and the repair (widen the item projection in `_live_item`, which both the direct and the snapshot payload paths read) is a deliverable the plan does not name.
findings.text: §3's mechanism is "`RECOVERY_CLASSIFICATION_DUTY_KINDS` gains an entry", but its done-when requires the obligation be listed "with its `next_action` and the refusal text"; `_live_item` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:727-736`) projects only `kind`, `run_id`, `node`, `plan`, `age_seconds` and `next_command`, and the refusal text lives in the row's `detail` (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1716-1723`), not in `next_action` ("repair the waiting declaration in … before resuming"), so a map-only change produces an item carrying no refusal text

findings.reason: the third run's recovery reading is `interrupted`, which the new entry never touches, so no mutation of the declared mechanism can make it appear twice; the case and its control should be replaced by one that can fail (for example, listing every waiting-or-unreadable run makes the second case, the valid probe, appear).
findings.text: §3's third case ("a run already listed as `turn-ended-early` is listed once") and its control ("skipping the de-duplication lists the third run twice") cannot fail: the obligations loop takes at most one kind per row through a single `if recovery_classification in …: … else: …` followed by one `items.append` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:1967-1972`), so no implementation of the declared mechanism can list a run twice and there is no de-duplication step to skip

response_events.note: §3 now covers exited-unfinished too: both classifications whose verb is repair are keyed, since an exited-unfinished run is owed nothing today.
